words: There was this old train in the snow at night, and my grandfather was across from me. He’s been gone for years, so that already felt weird.
He had a brown leather suitcase on his knees, like he was waiting to show me something. Outside everything was white and blue.
Yeah, he opened it. Full of letters, hundreds of them, and they were all addressed to me. He didn't say anything, just held it out so I could see.
I don’t remember what the handwriting looked like. It was more just the pile of envelopes, all with my name.
Yeah, I was just me, sitting across from him on the train. It felt very quiet, like the whole train was holding its breath.
The train stopped in the middle of a snowy field, and we both got off. We walked through deep snow toward a red door standing on its own, no house around it, just the frame.
It felt strange but also like it made sense in the dream. He gave me the suitcase and nodded at the door.
Yeah, I opened it. There was warm yellow light on the other side. That’s where it ended.
Probably the part where he opened the suitcase and showed me all those letters. That image stuck with me the most.
You got it right. That’s exactly how it went.
Yes, I would like that.
Watercolor feels closest, I think.
That sounds right to me, you can keep it that way.
Just however you imagine me, that’s fine.
It looks right to me.
That’s the moment that stuck with me.
It looks right. It has that quiet, blue-and-white feel from the dream.
I see, I’ll wait for the rest.
They look right so far. The suitcase full of letters and the empty field both match.
All six are there now. It’s the whole dream in order, and it looks right.
